title: Phoenix Labs is a Nested Contributor, contributing to both Spark and Sky at the same time
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.5 records that "Phoenix Labs is a development company that provides services to the Spark Foundation. Phoenix Labs is a *Nested Contributor*, i.e., a core contributor to both Spark and Sky."

The term is doing real work. In a structure where Agents have their own foundations, tokens and governance, the default assumption is that a contributor belongs to one layer. Nested Contributor names the case where the same organization is core to both, and treats it as a recognized status rather than an irregularity to be resolved.

What makes this consequential is that a Nested Contributor sits on both sides of transactions between Sky and the Agent — for example the terms on which Sky supplies liquidity to SparkLend. The Atlas's response is to label the dual role explicitly instead of prohibiting it, on the reasoning that visibility is more useful than a separation requirement that the ecosystem's actual talent distribution would defeat.

The pattern generalizes: where an ecosystem spawns semi-autonomous units from its own core team, contributor identity is layered, and naming the layering is a precondition for governing the conflicts it creates.
description: The Atlas names a role for organizations that serve an Agent and the parent ecosystem simultaneously, rather than forcing contributors to belong to exactly one entity.
